newsitem.title: UK: UK denies plan to make Clarke EU Commissioner.
newsitem.headline: UK denies plan to make Clarke EU Commissioner.

text.p: The British government on Monday denied a newspaper report that Prime Minister Tony Blair was about to offer former Conservative Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke a post as one of Britain's two European Commissioners.
"It's complete nonsense," a spokesman in Blair's office said of the report in the tabloid Sun.
The opposition Conservatives' representative on the Commission at present is Sir Leon Brittan, whose term of office expires in 1999. Britain's other commissioner is former Labour leader Neil Kinnock.
But the spokesman said the government has not yet given any consideration as to what should happen at the end of Brittan's term.
The Sun story followed a statement by Minister without Portfolio Peter Mandelson, reckoned one of Blair's right-hand men, praising Clarke's stance on European issues.

Mandelson said on Sunday that the Euro-friendly Clarke was "one of a minority of Conservatives who have a better understanding of Britain's long-term interests in Europe." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
